name: showreel-30-alive

voice.text: Why do the best apps feel alive? One: the heart pops, then wobbles into place. Two: the switch knob stretches as it slides. Three: the checkmark draws itself in. Save all three for your next app.

experiment.change: calm slow-mo details compilation (3 beats of ~5.9 s) in look C

caption:
Why do the best apps feel alive? ✨ Three tiny motions, each played at real speed, then slowed down so you can see it.

1) The heart pops, then wobbles into place: transition on scale with linear(), 450 ms.
2) The switch knob stretches as it slides: cubic-bezier(.34, 1.56, .64, 1) on translate, plus a squash keyframe on scale.
3) The checkmark draws itself in: stroke-dasharray and stroke-dashoffset on the tick's path, 400 ms.

linear() works in Chrome 113, Firefox 112 and Safari 17.2; the scale and translate properties in Chrome 104, Firefox 72 and Safari 14.1.
Save it for your next app, or send it to a designer friend.

sources.note: MDN, linear() easing (values past 1 overshoot); BCD: Chrome 113, Firefox 112, Safari 17.2
MDN, cubic-bezier(): y values may leave 0-1 (overshoot); BCD: Chrome 16, Firefox 4, Safari 6
MDN, stroke-dashoffset (CSS property, animatable by computed value); BCD: Chrome 1, Firefox 1.5, Safari 4
MDN, the scale and translate properties; BCD: Chrome 104, Firefox 72, Safari 14.1

tip.title: Three tiny motions that make an app feel alive
tip.why: A control that pops, stretches or draws reads as an answer to your finger; one that just switches state reads as a glitch. Each of these is one transition line.
